The shaded regions above represent the truth sets of predicates $P(x)$ and $Q(x),$ defined over the universal set ${R}^{2}.$ Which of the following is the truth set of $P(x)⇔Q(x)?$
worked_solution:
Since we have that 

$$
P(x)⇔Q(x)≡(P(x)∧Q(x))∨(¬P(x)∧¬Q(x)),
$$

 

the corresponding truth set can be found as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14099768/assets/0188e215f62afde3fa730642703fb6e2b213f8864f912ac0688d35fa29bb4db2.png)

Then, we sketch the set ${\overset{―}{T}}_{P}$ and ${\overset{―}{T}}_{Q}:$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14099768/assets/f4df9eb071e2deb4c79c8928a7b9e60f3341bba827a5fbb328e864d2de9a5803.png)

As a result, ${\overset{―}{T}}_{P}\cap {\overset{―}{T}}_{Q}$ is the following: 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14099768/assets/f17a4b0599a2dcc3d83d455c9be4e8a5033b7175c1859bfa634d2a3367553e0a.png)

Finally, to get the truth set of $P(x)⇔Q(x),$ we take all the points that belong to ${T}_{P}\cap {T}_{Q}$ or ${\overset{―}{T}}_{P}\cap {\overset{―}{T}}_{Q}:$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14099768/assets/4683bc52b9d18e7710b593d36ca191adeee6ecbc93428e1f40dd7161794090d8.png)
